name: Earthquake
description: Rapid safety assessment and decision tree for active tremors, structural damage, trapped persons, and post-shaking evacuation.

eq_start.prompt: Where are you currently located right now?
eq_start.context: Your physical location dictates the safest immediate action during seismic activity.

options.text: Inside a building (House / Apartment / Office)
options.description: You are within an enclosed residential or commercial structure.

options.text: Outdoors (Street / Open space / Alley)
options.description: You are currently outside in an open or urban area.

options.text: Inside a moving or stopped motor vehicle
options.description: You are driving or a passenger in a car, bus, or two-wheeler.

eq_indoor_status.prompt: What is the immediate situation inside the building?
eq_indoor_status.context: Assess whether ground shaking is actively occurring or if you have suffered structural collapse.

options.text: The ground / building is actively shaking right now
options.description: Violent or moderate shaking is in progress.

options.text: Shaking has stopped; inspecting structural integrity
options.description: Tremors have paused, but hazards or aftershocks are imminent.

options.text: Trapped under debris, rubble, or heavy furniture
options.description: You cannot exit freely or are pinned down by fallen objects.

eq_indoor_active_shaking.prompt: What type of cover or room features are immediately accessible within 2-3 steps?
eq_indoor_active_shaking.context: During active tremors, running across rooms or attempting stairs causes the majority of severe trauma injuries.

options.text: A sturdy wooden/metal table or heavy desk is nearby
options.description: Strong overhead shield available immediately.

options.text: No sturdy furniture nearby; only bare walls / bed / doorway
options.description: Open room with glass windows, false ceiling, or unreinforced walls.

eq_indoor_hazard_check.prompt: Shaking stopped. Are you detecting any utility hazards or severe building cracks?
eq_indoor_hazard_check.context: Secondary post-earthquake fires and building collapse cause extensive casualties.

options.text: Smell of gas leak, electrical sparking, or severed water lines
options.description: Immediate fire or electrocution hazard present.

options.text: No gas smell or fire, but stairs/exits need evaluation
options.description: Evaluating evacuation route to open ground.

eq_indoor_evacuation_choice.prompt: What floor are you on, and what is the state of your exit pathway?
eq_indoor_evacuation_choice.context: Aftershocks can trigger subsequent collapses of compromised structures.

options.text: Ground floor / 1st floor with clear unobstructed exit to open ground
options.description: Direct, rapid access to an open external assembly area.

options.text: Multi-story / high-rise building with stairwell access
options.description: Elevated floor where stair congestion and aftershocks must be managed.

eq_indoor_trapped_protocol.prompt: Assess your physical mobility and respiratory environment under the debris:
eq_indoor_trapped_protocol.context: Preserving oxygen, preventing dust inhalation, and signaling without exhaust are critical for survival.

options.text: Airway open, can tap objects or have a mobile/whistle
options.description: Able to generate auditory signals without inhaling toxic dust.

options.text: Dense dust, smoke, or constricted breathing space
options.description: Airway is at risk from plaster dust or smoke.

eq_outdoor_status.prompt: What are your immediate physical surroundings outdoors?
eq_outdoor_status.context: Falling glass, masonry, billboards, and downed electrical lines are the top outdoor seismic hazards.

options.text: High-density street with tall buildings, glass facades, or power poles
options.description: Surrounded by vertical structures prone to shedding debris.

options.text: Open field, wide park, sports ground, or open agricultural field
options.description: No overhead structures or power cables within striking radius.

options.text: Near steep hillsides, cliffs, road cuttings, or coastal shoreline
options.description: Risk of earthquake-triggered rockfall, landslide, or tsunami.

eq_outdoor_urban_hazards.prompt: Are live power cables down or is masonry actively falling from facades?
eq_outdoor_urban_hazards.context: Step potential from fallen electrical cables can electrocute you even at a distance.

options.text: Downed electrical cables or transformer sparks visible
options.description: Live electricity hazard on pavement or wet road.

options.text: Falling glass/parapets; need immediate trajectory protection
options.description: Shielding your head from overhead facade failure.

eq_vehicle_status.prompt: Where is the vehicle currently positioned on the roadway?
eq_vehicle_status.context: Bridges, flyovers, tunnels, and underpasses are highly susceptible to seismic shear failure.

options.text: On an overpass, flyover, bridge, or inside an underpass/tunnel
options.description: Elevated or subterranean road infrastructure.

options.text: Open highway or street, clear of overhanging signs and power lines
options.description: Flat ground clear of elevated structural hazards.

guidance.status: IMMEDIATE LIFE-SAFETY: DROP, COVER, AND HOLD ON
guidance.summary: You are indoors during active tremors with sturdy furniture accessible. Protect your vital organs immediately.
immediate_actions: DROP onto your hands and knees immediately to prevent being knocked over.
COVER your head and neck (and your entire body if possible) underneath the sturdy table or desk.
HOLD ON to your shelter with one hand and stay ready to move with it if it shifts.
Keep eyes closed and face buried against your chest or arm to protect against shattering glass.
Remain under cover until ground shaking has completely stopped for at least 60 seconds.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT run outside while the ground is shaking — falling tiles, bricks, and facade glass cause most injuries.
DO NOT stand in doorways; modern doorways are rarely load-bearing and do not shield against flying objects.
DO NOT use elevators under any circumstances.
DO NOT stand near windows, glass cabinets, heavy mirrors, or hanging chandeliers.
preventive_measures: After shaking halts, put on sturdy shoes immediately to protect against broken glass.
Inspect exits before attempting evacuation.
Anticipate strong aftershocks within minutes or hours.
guidance.official_reference: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) — National Earthquake Risk Mitigation Guidelines

guidance.summary: No furniture is available. Drop along an interior load-bearing partition wall far from exterior windows.
immediate_actions: DROP immediately to the floor against an interior wall away from exterior windows, mirrors, and tall furniture.
Crouch low, facing the interior wall, and interlock your fingers behind your neck to protect the cervical spine.
Pull your elbows against your knees to form a compact protective triangle.
If on a bed and cannot move, stay face down and pull pillows over your head and neck.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT run towards stairs or balcony railing.
DO NOT attempt to retrieve personal belongings or electronics while shaking is active.
DO NOT light matches, candles, or lighters due to potential gas leaks.
preventive_measures: When shaking stops, scan your ceiling for sagging structural plaster.
Locate your emergency 72-hour go-bag if within immediate reach.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA India & Standard Operating Procedure for Earthquake Management

guidance.summary: Gas leak or electrical arcing detected post-quake. Prevent immediate ignition or explosion.
immediate_actions: Turn off the primary gas cylinder valve (LPG regulator) or main gas line valve immediately if safely accessible.
Switch off the main electrical breaker ONLY if the switchboard is completely dry and safe to touch.
Open exterior doors and windows to vent volatile gas vapors if doing so takes seconds.
Evacuate everyone immediately to an open outdoor space via stairs (never elevators).
Alert neighbors verbally while exiting without ringing electrical doorbells.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT flip light switches, use flashlights with spark switches, or use corded phones.
DO NOT light lighters, matches, or stoves.
DO NOT attempt to enter flooded basements where electrical currents may be energized.
preventive_measures: Once outdoors at a safe distance (at least 50m), dial 112 or Fire 101 to report the gas leak.
Never re-enter a gas-filled structure until authorized by certified emergency personnel.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Post-Earthquake Fire Safety & Hazardous Material Protocols

guidance.status: ORDERLY EVACUATION TO OPEN ASSEMBLY ZONE
guidance.summary: Shaking has halted and ground exit is unobstructed. Evacuate immediately before aftershocks.
immediate_actions: Put on sturdy shoes or boots to prevent lacerations from shattered debris.
Grab your emergency Go-Bag (water, torch, first aid, medicines) if it is immediately at hand.
Evacuate through the exterior door calmly without pushing.
Move at least 1.5 times the height of adjacent buildings into an open field or designated park.
Stay alert for falling roof tiles, chimney bricks, and air-conditioning units.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT loiter on sidewalks, under awnings, or below power transmission lines.
DO NOT re-enter the building to search for pets or valuables until officially declared safe.
DO NOT spread unverified rumors on social media or tie up phone lines; use SMS for emergency contacts.
preventive_measures: Perform a headcount of family/group members in the open assembly area.
Check everyone for injuries and administer basic first aid if trained.

guidance.summary: You are on an elevated floor. Proceed down stairwells cautiously; beware jam-packed landings and aftershocks.
immediate_actions: Check the stairwell door with the back of your hand before opening to detect heat from secondary fires.
Descend the staircase along the inner rail, moving deliberately and allowing space for emergency responders.
If an aftershock begins while on the stairs, crouch on the landing against the inner wall and protect your head.
Follow instructions from building wardens and move directly out to open street areas once ground level is reached.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT use elevators — power failure can trap you in elevator shafts between floors.
DO NOT crowd or push down stairs; stampedes are a major source of post-quake trauma.
DO NOT climb onto the roof unless ground exits are blocked by intense fire or collapse.
preventive_measures: Report any visible shearing or diagonal X-cracks in concrete columns to municipal authorities.
Keep stairwell doors unlocked from inside to prevent trapping subsequent evacuees.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA High-Rise Building Seismic Safety Directives

guidance.summary: Trapped under debris with intact airway. Conserve physical energy and oxygen while signaling rescuers.
immediate_actions: Cover your mouth and nose with a handkerchief, clothing cloth, or mask to filter pulverized cement and dust.
Tap on a metal pipe, radiator, or structural wall with a stone or piece of rubble in rhythmic bursts of 3 (SOS signal).
Use a whistle if one is on your keychain or emergency kit — whistle sounds carry through rubble better than voices.
Only shout as a last resort when you clearly hear search teams or rescue dogs working directly overhead.
Keep calm to reduce oxygen consumption and heart rate.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT shout continuously — screaming causes dust inhalation, vocal cord damage, and rapid exhaustion.
DO NOT strike matches or lighters — risk of igniting leaking domestic gas.
DO NOT make sudden jerky movements that could destabilize overhead debris or concrete slabs.
preventive_measures: If your phone has signal, send a brief SMS/WhatsApp text with your last known floor/room coordinates.
Turn phone screen brightness to minimum to preserve battery for emergency location beaconing.
guidance.official_reference: NDRF Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) Survival Guidelines

guidance.summary: Trapped with heavy dust and smoke. Immediate protection of airway and vital organs is paramount.
immediate_actions: Pull your shirt over your nose and mouth; breathe shallowly through your nose to avoid inhaling abrasive silica dust.
Keep head protected with any cushion, jacket, or your arms tucked over the skull.
Listen carefully for quiet periods in rescue operations when listening devices are deployed.
Tap three times on solid debris every few minutes to make your presence audible to acoustic listening sensors.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT panic or hyperventilate; carbon dioxide buildup in confined voids can cause loss of consciousness.
DO NOT attempt to kick away heavy structural pillars or beams supporting the void.
preventive_measures: Remain patient; USAR rescue teams systematically search rubble with sniffer dogs, acoustic sensors, and cameras.
guidance.official_reference: International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) & NDMA SOP

guidance.summary: Downed electrical cables pose extreme electrocution risk via step potential through the ground.
immediate_actions: Maintain at least 10 meters (33 feet) distance from all fallen power lines and any objects touching them.
If trapped near a line, keep feet together and bunny-hop or shuffle without lifting your feet to avoid ground gradient current.
Warn pedestrians and vehicles to stay clear immediately.
Report the fallen power line immediately to 112 and local electricity board.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT touch puddles of water, chain-link fences, metal guardrails, or vehicles touching downed cables.
DO NOT attempt to push wires away with sticks, broom handles, or umbrellas — high voltage arcs through dry wood.
preventive_measures: Wait for certified electrical utility linemen to de-energize the feeder before approaching the zone.
guidance.official_reference: Central Electricity Authority (Safety Requirements) & NDMA Safety Code

guidance.summary: Outdoor urban canyon with falling facade tiles, window glass, and air conditioners.
immediate_actions: Protect your head and neck immediately using a backpack, briefcase, jacket, or your interlocked arms.
Move swiftly into the center of a wide road or open courtyard away from building perimeters.
If nowhere open is reachable, take refuge inside a solid archway or under a sturdy bus shelter structure.
Watch for traffic as vehicles may drive erratically due to pavement buckling.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT seek shelter under cantilevered balconies, glass canopies, or overhead advertising hoardings.
DO NOT rush to enter buildings to escape the street; doorways have high falling object casualty rates.
preventive_measures: Locate open municipal parks or school sports grounds designated as civil defense assembly points.

guidance.summary: You are in an open field, park, or wide ground. This is the safest outdoor position during an earthquake.
immediate_actions: Stay in the open ground until all shaking has stopped completely.
Crouch low if ground motion is violent enough to unbalance you.
Look around to verify no overhead utility cables or leaning trees are nearby.
Assist individuals who may be disoriented or injured, offering basic reassurance and first aid.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT rush back inside buildings to check on property or pets.
DO NOT block access roads needed by emergency fire and ambulance vehicles.
preventive_measures: Tune in to official emergency broadcasts via All India Radio (AIR) or official disaster management channels on phone.
Prepare for potential aftershocks over the next 24 to 72 hours.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Guidelines for Disaster Awareness & Community Response

guidance.summary: Earthquakes in hilly terrain trigger rockfalls and landslides; along the coast, they can generate devastating tsunamis.
immediate_actions: If near steep cliffs or hill slopes: Move immediately away from the base or crest of the slope to avoid rockfall.
If near the sea/beach: An earthquake shaking the ground is your natural warning. Move immediately inland and to high ground (at least 15m elevation or 1-2 km inland).
Do not wait for formal sirens or official announcements if you felt strong shaking near the coast.
Stay on high ground until disaster management authorities give official all-clear.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT walk down to the coast to watch receding seawater or explore exposed seabed.
DO NOT shelter directly beneath unstable highway road cuts or steep retaining walls.
preventive_measures: Follow marked Tsunami / Landslide Evacuation Routes where installed by local administration.
guidance.official_reference: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) & NDMA Guidelines

guidance.summary: Flyovers, elevated expressways, bridges, and tunnels are high-vulnerability structures during seismic tremors.
immediate_actions: If safely possible without colliding, drive off the bridge, flyover, or out of the underpass immediately.
If traffic is stopped or the deck is buckled, pull the vehicle as far to the shoulder as possible.
Turn on emergency hazard warning blinkers and set the emergency handbrake.
Turn off the engine, leave the keys in the ignition or console (for emergency crane towing), and exit the vehicle.
Walk calmly along the bridge walkway toward the nearest stable abutment or ramp off the structure.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT park directly beneath overhead sign gantries, street light poles, or concrete expansion joints.
DO NOT abandon your vehicle in the middle lane where it blocks fire engines and rescue ambulances.
preventive_measures: Once on stable ground, move well away from highway overpass pillars.
guidance.official_reference: Indian Roads Congress (IRC) & NDMA Transport Safety Directives

guidance.summary: You are driving on an open roadway. Stop safely away from road hazards and remain inside.
immediate_actions: Slow down gradually and pull over to the side of the road safely out of the traffic flow.
Ensure you are clear of power poles, tall hoardings, overhanging trees, and fuel stations.
Put the vehicle in Park (or neutral with handbrake engaged) and turn on hazard flashers.
Remain inside the vehicle — the metal shell and suspension offer protection from flying debris.
Listen to vehicle car radio for emergency civil defense updates.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT stop abruptly in the middle of active traffic.
DO NOT exit the vehicle if power lines have fallen across the hood or roof; the tires insulate you, but stepping out creates a path to ground.
preventive_measures: Proceed with extreme caution only after shaking stops completely, watching for buckled asphalt, sinkholes, and fallen debris.
